playbook.strategy: In ta_winasmuch, the win condition is highest individual total including reserves, and burning is overwhelmingly dominant: 1 point of self-cost for 12 points of rival damage, with no pick resolution on burn turns so rivals cannot retaliate. Burn every round until rivals' reserves are drained, then close at the first legal round (round 3) to lock in the lead — this produced a +6.0 win versus rivals at 0. Watch for variants where burn is limited, reserves are individual rather than shared, or closing is delayed; if burning is unavailable, the pick game against Y-starting mirroring rivals favors picking X (one X earns 3 while each Y loses 1), but I have not yet observed the mirroring behavior directly. General lesson: when a game offers an action that damages rivals more than it costs me and bypasses the main mechanic, check whether it can be repeated every turn — the stated payoff matrix may be a decoy. Preserve the Hanabi lessons: clue only the exact next-rank single card, verify stack+1 before spending tokens, budget non-refreshing resources, and close out a won position at the earliest legal opportunity.
